The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice G. Anupama Chakravarthy
 Criminal Petition No.2016 Of 2023
O R D E R:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure (for short 'Cr.P.C.')
by the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 3 to quash the proceedings against them in C.C.No.1722 of 2020 on the file of XVII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad at Malkajgiri, for the offences under Sections 406, 420, 447, 427 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').
2.

entities.text: XVII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad at Malkajgiri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Sri A.Jagan, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri S.Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1-State and Sri M.Ratan Singh, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the record.

3. The brief facts, culled out from the charge sheet, are that this is a case of Cheating by grabbing the land admeasuring Ac.0.03 gts of land in Sy.Nos.18 & 89 situated at Ahmedguda Village, wherein the father of respondent No.2 is the owner of land admeasuring Ac.1.20 gts in the said Survey numbers and the petitioner No.1 is the owner of land admeasuring Ac.1.00 gts in Sy.No.19/2 vide document No 3342/1981.

The father of respondent No.2 and petitioner No.1 started a Rice Mill in the GAC, J Crlp_2016_2023 name and Style of Sri Vijaya Venkataramana Binny Rice Mill in Ahmedguda Village by entering a partnership and by obtaining loan from the Hyderabad District Co-operative Central Bank.
Thereafter, the two brothers of petitioners No.1 i.e., petitioners No.2 and 3 were joined as partners into his 50% Share.
The said firm run up to 2013 and thereafter, it was defunct.
Thereafter, respondent No.2 got his share of land in to his possession, while petitioner No.1 has taken his share of land admeasuring Ac.1.00 gts.

Later, the petitioners hatched a plan to grab the land admeasuring Ac. 0.03 gts and taken the pass book for the land admeasuring Ac.1.03 gts instead of Ac.1.00 gts by breaching the trust of respondent No.2.
Having known the same, respondent No.2 put the same into the notice of the MRO, rectified the same in revenue records, and arranged boundary pillars around his land by arranging watchman.

While the matter stood thus, on 14.02.2020, the petitioners No.1 and 2 criminally trespassed into the land of respondent No.2,
bulldogged his Compound wall and caused huge loss to him.
Basing on the same, a case in FIR No.85 of 2020 on the file of the Station House Officer, Kesara Police Station, Rachakonda, was registered against the petitioners.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the father of respondent No.2 has given an affidavit to the petitioners GAC, J Crlp_2016_2023 transferring the land in favour of the petitioners, for which, they got mutated the land to Ac.1.03 guntas instead of Ac.1.00.

Furthermore,
as per the contents of the complaint, the case is purely civil in nature and the ingredients of the offences alleged against the petitioners are not at all attracted.
Therefore, prayed to quash the proceedings against them.

sentences.text: 1 5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 filed a detailed counter contending that respondent No.2 is the absolute owner of the land and the petitioners by suppressing the said fact have mutated Ac.0.03 guntas in their favour.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently opposed to quash the proceedings against the petitioners and contended that it is not a fit case to be quashed.
Therefore, prayed to dismiss the Criminal Petition.

6. On perusal of the entire record, it is evident that one G.Ramachandraiah, who is the late father of respondent No.2, purchased the land admeasuring Ac.1.20 gts in Sy.Nos.18 & 89 situated at Ahmedguda Village, which is an undisputed fact by both the parties.

It is the specific contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the father of respondent No.2 has given an affidavit for transferring the said land in the name of the petitioners and the petitioners are the absolute owners of the land.
GAC, J Crlp_2016_2023

But, as per Transfer of Property Act, immovable properties cannot be transferred by way of an affidavit, there should be a regular sale deed to that effect and basing on the regular sale deed alone, mutation can be done.
In the present case, there is no regular sale deed, in favour of the petitioners, to the extent of land admeasuring Ac.0.03 guntas.

Further, the record reveals that respondent No.2 has brought to the notice of MRO for rectification of the same in revenue records and thereafter, arranged boundary pillars around his land by arranging a watchman.
Furthermore, the statement of the watchman recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., clearly discloses that the petitioners have trespassed into the subject land and demolished the compound wall.
Admittedly, it is a matter of fact to be decided by way of trial before the trial Court to prove the innocence of the petitioners.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that it is not a fit case to quash the proceedings against the petitioners at this juncture and the Criminal Petition is liable to be dismissed.
7. The Criminal Petition is devoid of merits and the same is accordingly dismissed.
GAC, J Crlp_2016_2023 Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.

G.ANUPAMA CHAKRAVARTHY, J Date:
19.09.2023 TMK GAC, J Crlp_2016_2023
THE HON'BLE SMT.
